checked_sources.source: Saha & Ramdas 2026, Non-partitioned e-detectors for nonparametric sequential change detection, arXiv:2607.28322
checked_sources.result: Retained as the exact composite-null reference architecture: candidate-start evidence is aggregated and then minimized over candidate no-change laws; exact all-start evaluation has history-growing computation, motivating a lower-cost architecture without weakening false-alarm semantics.

checked_sources.source: Xie et al. 2022, Window-Limited CUSUM for Sequential Change Detection, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory / arXiv:2206.06777
checked_sources.result: Independent precedent for exposing a minimum signal/information scale as a design parameter. WLCUSUM is first-order optimal with w growing slower than log(gamma), fastest convergence at w on the order of sqrt(log gamma); a parallel-window construction handles unknown optimal window with explicit threshold/complexity cost. The paper also notes that a preset lower bound on information can oversize the window and delay detection.

checked_sources.source: Kotłowski & Grünwald 2011, Maximum Likelihood vs. Sequential Normalized Maximum Likelihood in On-line Density Estimation, PMLR 19
checked_sources.result: For Gaussian exponential families the cumulative SNML regret after initialization is logarithmic; fixed-variance Gaussian gives explicit k/2 log n behavior, and unknown mean/variance has per-round increment 1/n+O(n^-2). Initial unrestricted Gaussian prediction remains singular, so a proper burn-in predictor remains necessary.

checked_sources.source: Malik & Bansal 2022, Sequential Change Detection through Empirical Distribution and Universal Codes, arXiv:2112.07549
checked_sources.result: Provides direct precedent for separating an initial pre-change training estimate from a universal post-change code. Its delay scales with the divergence gap after accounting for pre-change estimation error, supporting a frozen-anchor rather than a continuously contaminated baseline architecture.

checked_sources.source: Moen 2025/2026, A grid-based methodology for fast online changepoint detection, arXiv:2504.09573
checked_sources.result: Sparse geometric split grids can reduce online changepoint update/storage growth to logarithmic for broad offline statistics while retaining nonasymptotic delay guarantees under the paper's assumptions. This supports a multiscale sparse-start fallback rather than dense all-start enumeration.

derived_results.claim: The r65 equal-variance pair-balance heuristic admits a direct finite-sample high-probability lower bound with separate universal-code regret terms.
derived_results.scope: Pure prefix X_1:T iid N(0,1), pure local block Y_1:n iid N(delta,1), candidate no-change law R_mu=N(mu,1). Predictive codes q_- and q_+ satisfy pathwise log-regret bounds r_T and r_n relative to the true block laws.
derived_results.derivation: Let I=delta^2/2, eta in (0,1), x=log(4/eta), and kappa in (0,1). On the event |sum_i X_i|<=sqrt(2Tx) and |sum_j(Y_j-delta)|<=sqrt(2nx), which has probability at least 1-eta by Gaussian tails and a union bound, Young's inequality gives simultaneously for every mu: A_T(mu)=log q_-(X_1:T)-log p_mu(X_1:T) >= (1-kappa)T mu^2/2-r_T-x/kappa, and B_n(mu)>= (1-kappa)n(delta-mu)^2/2-r_n-x/kappa. Hence with R=max(r_T,r_n)+x/kappa, inf_mu max{A_T(mu),B_n(mu)} >= (1-kappa) I*T*n/(sqrt(T)+sqrt(n))^2 - R. This is a conservative theorem-level version of the r65 pair-balance equation rather than a mean-drift heuristic.

derived_results.claim: The finite-sample pair bound yields a closed-form sufficient local lifetime and exposes a hard finite-prefix weak-change capacity limit.
derived_results.derivation: For alarm log-threshold L=log A, define B=(L+R)/((1-kappa)I). A sufficient condition is T*n/(sqrt(T)+sqrt(n))^2 >= B. If B<T, inversion gives n >= n_star = B/(1-sqrt(B/T))^2. If B>=T the bound cannot certify any finite n. When T>>B, n_star=B+2B^(3/2)/sqrt(T)+O(B^2/T); as B approaches T, n_star diverges. Thus H approximately L/I is not a reliable finite-sample sizing rule when the prefix is not very long relative to the evidence requirement.

derived_results.claim: End-to-end repeated-retry simulation confirms that the finite-threshold failure diagnosed in r65 persists beyond first-expiry scoring and is strongly information-rate dependent.

details.scope: Synthetic fixed-variance Gaussian mean shifts with a proper per-start universal predictor: first sample Cauchy(0,1), subsequent fixed-variance Gaussian SNML predictions N(previous mean,k/(k-1)). Sparse detector uses live-prefix plus rolling-local pair evidence and repeated local retries. These are numerical engineering checks, not statistical guarantees.
details.A_1e6_Tpre500_delta2_Tpost200_30_common_: H in {23,60,120}: all 30/30 paths detected with zero observed pre-change false alarms; median delay 13 and q90 about 19 across these tested H values.
details.interpretation: A moderate shift (I=0.5) needs materially longer-lived retries than the original H=23 threshold-scaled bank, while a strong shift (I=2) is easy. Zero empirical false alarms in this small experiment must not be interpreted as a formal ARL/PFA result.

derived_results.claim: A stronger architecture is to freeze the pre-change anchor at each candidate split and compare one stationary no-change law against two independently reset universal predictive codes, rather than continuing a live prefix through post-change contamination.
derived_results.derivation: For deterministic/predictable split s, define q^(s)(x_1:t)=q^-(x_1:s-1) q^+_s(x_s:t), where each factor is a proper sequential predictive density and q^+ is reset at s. For any fixed no-change R, M^(R)_{s,t}=q^(s)(X_1:t)/p_R(X_1:t) is a likelihood-ratio martingale/e-process under R because q^(s) is itself a proper joint sequential density. In the known-variance Gaussian pure-block case, separate regret yields expected information T mu^2/2+n(delta-mu)^2/2-(r_T+r_n); minimizing over mu gives I*T*n/(T+n), strictly stronger than the live max-pair term I*T*n/(sqrt(T)+sqrt(n))^2. On the same Gaussian concentration event, a conservative finite-sample form is inf_mu[A_T(mu)+B_n(mu)] >= (1-kappa)I*T*n/(T+n) - (r_T+r_n+2x/kappa). Defining C=(L+r_T+r_n+2x/kappa)/((1-kappa)I), a sufficient local length is n>=C*T/(T-C) when C<T. Operational composite-null start aggregation/ARL-PFA control has not yet been proved for this segmented architecture, so this is a candidate, not a deployed replacement.

derived_results.claim: An explicit information-floor hierarchy is preferable to relying on asymptotics to discover the needed lifetime, and WLCUSUM provides independent precedent for a minimum-signal design barrier.
derived_results.derivation: Use floors I_j=I_max*2^-j and choose each lifetime from the finite-sample inversion rather than H proportional only to log A. With spacing g_j approximately epsilon*H_j, each scale keeps O(1/epsilon) live starts, so J scales require O(J/epsilon) history-independent state. A change whose oracle evidence length lies near one scale pays at most roughly one spacing interval before a scheduled start. If every scale is merely a lower-surrogate over the same underlying full e-detector processes, taking their maximum remains pathwise below the full statistic and does not by itself require a multiplicity threshold; genuinely different predictor families/statistics do require weighting or other multiplicity control.

candidates_new.mechanism: At each sparse candidate split, freeze the pre-change universal predictor and independently reset a post-change universal predictor. Compare their product joint density to a single stationary no-change law. Aggregate sparse starts only after proving composite-null ARL/PFA semantics.
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: Known-variance Gaussian information term improves from the live max-pair I*T*n/(sqrt(T)+sqrt(n))^2 to product-segmented I*T*n/(T+n) before regret/concentration penalties; Malik-Bansal provides independent trained-baseline/universal-post precedent, while the likelihood-ratio construction gives point-null martingale validity for each fixed split and null law.
candidates_new.scope: Point-null validity and the pure-block Gaussian finite-sample information calculation are derived here. Composite-null aggregation, start weighting, unknown-variance initialization/regret, and matched ARL/PFA experiments remain open.
candidates_new.confidence: medium-high as an architecture candidate; insufficient for deployment until composite-null/start-aggregation proof closes.

candidates_new.mechanism: Maintain logarithmically many minimum-information scales, size each lifetime using the finite-sample certificate, and sparsify start times proportional to each lifetime. Route weaker changes to longer-lived scales instead of making one scale cover all I.
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: Finite-sample inversion gives explicit blow-up as required evidence B approaches finite prefix T; WLCUSUM independently uses a minimum signal/information barrier and parallel windows to adapt unknown optimal window. State can be O(J/epsilon) for J dyadic scales under proportional spacing.
candidates_new.scope: State bound is architectural. Constant-factor delay and pathwise false-alarm preservation need a theorem for the exact sparse segmented statistic chosen for deployment.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Repeated retries rescue the original H=23 live-prefix bank for moderate I at A=10^6.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected in the tested Gaussian setting: only 4/30 delta=1 paths were detected within 500 post-change samples at H=23, versus 30/30 at H=300. Strong delta=2 shifts were easy even at H=23, confirming information-rate sensitivity rather than a generic retry failure.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: H approximately log(A)/I is sufficient once a start survives long enough.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Still unsupported as a finite-sample engineering rule. The explicit pair inversion includes prefix-capacity, concentration and regret penalties and diverges as required normalized evidence approaches T; r65/r66 simulations show substantially larger H can be needed.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: All multiscale adaptation can be made threshold-free.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Too broad. No extra multiplicity charge is justified only when scales are pathwise lower-surrogates of the same full detector/statistic. Independent detector families or separately calibrated predictor variants need weights, union/e-value mixture control, or another valid multiplicity construction.

frontier: Prove composite-null ARL/PFA control for the frozen-anchor segmented universal-code e-process when aggregating sparse candidate splits, including valid start weights and the interaction with the outer infimum over no-change laws.

Extend the product-segment finite-sample lower bound from known variance to Gaussian unknown mean/variance with an explicit proper initialization quantile and logarithmic SNML regret; express the result in KL/information-radius form where possible.

Implement the frozen-anchor detector and run matched false-alarm/ARL plus detection-delay Monte Carlo against the live-prefix pair and exact all-start detector with at least hundreds of common-random paths rather than the current 30-path engineering check.

Formalize a dyadic information-floor bank with spacing proportional to lifetime and prove the state-versus-delay approximation factor; distinguish nested lower-surrogate scales from genuinely distinct detector families that need multiplicity control.
Stress variance-only and joint mean/variance changes, where mean-shift I=delta^2/2 is no longer an adequate observable information proxy.

actions_taken_instead_of_stopping: Converted the r65 pair-balance heuristic into an explicit high-probability finite-sample lower bound with separate code-regret penalties.
Inverted the bound to obtain a closed-form lifetime requirement and a finite-prefix capacity condition.
Ran repeated-retry stopping-time Monte Carlo, confirming weak/moderate information-rate failures persist beyond first-expiry scoring.
Derived a frozen-anchor segmented product e-process candidate that avoids live-prefix contamination and has a stronger Gaussian information term.
Connected explicit information-floor/multiscale sizing to independent WLCUSUM and sparse-grid changepoint precedents.

exact_next_action: Construct the frozen-anchor segmented universal-code detector as a proper point-null e-process for each split, prove its composite-null sparse-start aggregation and ARL/PFA theorem, then run matched false-alarm Monte Carlo against the live-prefix pair and exact all-start detector; only if those checks pass should it replace the live-prefix weak-change fallback.
